class.name: FellowRain3D
class.brief_description: Rain around the camera and wet surfaces where it falls: darker, glossier materials and puddles with ripples (FellowEngine).
class.description: Drops fall in a box of [member area] around the current camera (GPU particles: streaks aligned with their velocity, [member wind] included), stop where they hit the scene as seen from above and splash there ([member splashes]). While the node is active, the Forward+ renderer wets every opaque material after the material's own code ([code]fragment()[/code] of a [ShaderMaterial] too), in the depth pre-pass as well as the colour pass so screen-space and other reflections see the result: by [member wetness], porous surfaces (rough, not metallic) darken, all of them get a glossy film, and on flat rough ground puddles form ([member puddles]): flat, smooth standing water with the rain's ripples ([member ripple_tile], [member ripple_strength]). Undersides and surfaces under a roof stay dry: the scene's top seen from above (a [GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D] of [member occlusion_size] following the camera, the drops' collider) tells where the rain reaches. A [FellowWater3D] shows the ripples on its surface too. Transparent materials are not wetted. One node at a time is active: the last one to enter the tree. Wetness can follow the rain over time ([member wetness_follows_rain]). [code]rendering/fellow/fluid/enabled[/code] off turns the wetting off. The drops and the heightfield are internal children ([method get_drops], [method get_occlusion]). Decision record [code]docs/decisions/0124-rain.md[/code].

method.name: get_drops
method.description: The internal particles of the drops (their sub-emitter makes the splashes).

method.name: get_occlusion
method.description: The internal heightfield of the scene seen from above: the drops collide with it and surfaces below its top stay dry. Its [member GPUParticlesCollisionHeightField3D.heightfield_mask] picks the layers that shelter.

method.name: get_ripple_texture
method.description: The rain's ripples on standing water: a tiling texture of [member ripple_tile] (slopes in red and green, with mipmaps), computed every frame while the node is active.

members.member: The side of the box around the camera the drops fall in, in metres.
The colour of the drops (unshaded; alpha is their opacity at the middle of a streak). The splashes are twice as opaque.
A drop's streak in metres: width and length (the path a frame's exposure sees). Drops fade in from 0.5 m to 4 m from the camera.
The falling speed of the drops, in metres per second (the terminal speed of a raindrop of a few millimetres).
With [member wetness_follows_rain], the seconds a fully wet scene takes to dry once the rain stops.
The height above the camera the drops start from, in metres.
The number of drops at full [member rain]; [member rain] scales the number drawn.
If [code]true[/code], the heightfield of the scene seen from above is rendered again every frame (for moving roofs: vehicles, doors); otherwise when it moves with the camera.
The height of the heightfield's box, in metres, centred on the node's height.
The resolution of the heightfield (256 to 4096 texels a side). With the default [member occlusion_size], 1024 is 8 cm a texel.
The side of the heightfield around the camera, in metres. Beyond it everything is exposed to the rain.
How much of flat, rough ground is covered by puddles once it is wet (0: none, 1: nearly all).
How hard it rains (0 to 1): the number of drops, the ripples on standing water and, with [member wetness_follows_rain], how fast surfaces get wet.
A scale of the ripples' slopes on puddles and on wet flat ground.
The size in metres of the tile of the ripple texture (two offset lookups hide the repeat).
If [code]true[/code], drops splash where they land (two small droplets each, a sub-emitter at collision).
If [code]true[/code], the ripples' time advances with the process time; otherwise it is set by the [code]time[/code] property (deterministic renders).
How wet surfaces exposed to the rain are (0 to 1). Puddles appear above 0.4.
If [code]true[/code], [member wetness] grows while it rains (in [member wetting_time] at full rain) and falls when it does not (in [member drying_time]).
With [member wetness_follows_rain], the seconds full rain takes to make a dry scene fully wet.
The wind carrying the drops, in metres per second: their streaks lean with it and they start upwind of the camera so they land around it.
